Ricky Nelson wasn't just a kid who was made into a teen idol. Sure he had the good looks of a movie star, and did some film work, but foremost he was a musician. He played guitar, wrote some of his own songs, and he had a great baritone voice with excellent range.
Nelson was also one of the earliest movers in Country Rock in the 1960s, before it blossomed in the 1970s.
Ricky Nelson helped make early Rock & Roll popular, and then contributed to its evolution.

Suggesting that Nelson "cannily captured the idiomatic feel of contemporary country," biographer and music critic Joel Selvin wrote, "Artistically, Bright Lights served as a stunning reversal of field."

Although Nelson's move into straight country music didn't result in notable commercial gains, it made sense given that his prior few rock albums hadn't done much, and that most rockabilly performers had long since gone into the country market.
